title: Why does send() throw on a new WebSocket but not after close()?
checkedAgainst: Node's own WebSocket, the global one, run in `model.test.ts` against the small server in `oracle/socket.ts`, which accepts the handshake and answers close only when told: every state the live step's buttons reach (23 from a new socket, 14 from the open one) and every event from each is run on a real socket, comparing readyState, whether send() threw and its error's name, the open and close events, and which messages reached the server once the connection ended. The page's two opening programs run as written, and the code panel's lines are found, in order, in `WebSocket.prototype.send.toString()`.

grounding.sentence: Checked live, each time the model’s tests run, against Node's own WebSocket, against a local server (undici 7.30.1 in Node 24.22.1 when written).

answer: send() sends only in OPEN: before open it throws InvalidStateError, and after close() it quietly sends nothing

questions.question: In the open handler you call ws.close() and then ws.close() again. What does the second close() do?
questions.answer: Nothing: the first close() made readyState CLOSING, and close() does nothing in CLOSING or CLOSED. It does not throw, and the socket stays CLOSING.

questions.question: Before the socket opens, you wrap send() in try/catch so the error cannot crash the page. Once the open event fires, does the message go out?
questions.answer: No. The throw means send() did nothing: no message waits for later, so once open fires the server has received 0 messages until you call send() again.

scenarios.name: When send() is called: Right after close()

steps.title: What does this send() do?
steps.caption: Your socket opens, and its open handler sends "hi", calls ws.close(), then calls ws.send("bye") on the next line. Does that last send() throw, send the message, or return without sending it?

state.server: The server accepted, so open fired

server.after: The server accepted, so open fired

steps.picture: Code, 6 lines; The server accepted, so open fired. Asked about: 5: ws.send("bye").

steps.title: Answer: no error, and nothing is sent
steps.line: close() made it CLOSING at once, and send() returns there.
steps.caption: send() sends only in OPEN: before open it throws InvalidStateError, and after close() it quietly sends nothing. close() moves readyState from OPEN to CLOSING at once, before the server answers, so send()'s second check returns at the boxed line: no error, and the server has only "hi".

steps.line: Press send() or close(): neither changes anything now.
steps.caption: The server answers the close frame, the ring walks to CLOSED and the close event fires. send() returns quietly here too, so code that must not lose a message checks ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN before it sends.
